source.titleEnglishInternal: Coach Your Niece to Order Café de Olla Alone
source.objectiveEnglishInternal: Coach a teenager to order café de olla and a pan dulce on her own, with clear tips about the hot clay cup.
source.speakingEnglishInternal: You are the aunt or uncle, and the AI is your 15-year-old niece Sofi: coach her to order café de olla and a pan dulce on her own, using commands with pronouns like pídelo, agárralo por el asa and no lo toques todavía.
grammarEnglishExamplesInternal: If it's very hot, leave it on the table for a little while.
Pick a pan de yema and ask doña Eustolia for it.
source.readerTitleSpanish: Sofi pide sola en la fonda

readerVerbExamples.target: Pídelo sin piloncillo si no lo quieres tan dulce.
readerVerbExamples.native: Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.

readerVerbExamples.target: Agárralo por el asa, nunca por el borde.

readerVerbExamples.native: Taste it slowly, because the clay holds the heat.

archivedDraft.scene: An adult coaches a teenager to order a hot cocoa and bread at a café counter.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Pídelo sin piloncillo si no lo quieres tan dulce.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: あまり甘くないのがよければ、ピロンシージョなしで頼んでね。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Agárralo por el asa, nunca por el borde.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Hold it by the handle, never by the rim.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 取っ手を持って。マグのふちは絶対に持たないでね。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Hold it by the handle, never by the rim.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: No lo toques todavía; espera a que deje de echar vapor.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Don't touch it yet; wait until it stops steaming.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: まだ触らないで。湯気が出なくなるまで待ってね。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Don't touch it yet; wait until it stops steaming.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Pruébalo despacito, porque el barro guarda el calor.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Taste it slowly, because the clay holds the heat.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: ゆっくり少しずつ味わってね。陶器の器は熱を保つから。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Taste it slowly, because the clay holds the heat.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Salúdala primero y háblale de usted.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Greet her first and speak to her formally.
sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Use usted with older vendors as a sign of respect.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: まずあいさつして、それから丁寧な言葉で話しかけてね。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Greet her first and speak to her formally.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Pregúntale cuánto es y págale con el billete de 50.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Ask her how much it is and pay her with the 50-peso bill.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: いくらか聞いて、50ペソ札で払ってね。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Ask her how much it is and pay her with the 50-peso bill.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Buenos días, doña Eustolia, ¿me da un café de olla?
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Good morning, doña Eustolia, may I have a café de olla?
sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Formal; doña goes before a first name.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: おはようございます、ドニャ・エウストリア。カフェ・デ・オジャを一杯いただけますか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Good morning, doña Eustolia, may I have a café de olla?

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Tú puedes, yo te espero aquí en la banca.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: You've got this, I'll wait for you here on the bench.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: ソフィならできるよ。私はここのベンチで待ってるね。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: You've got this, I'll wait for you here on the bench.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: La tía Carmen y su sobrina Sofi, de 15 años, llegan temprano a una fonda del mercado de Oaxaca.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Aunt Carmen and her niece Sofi, 15 years old, arrive early at a small eatery in the Oaxaca market.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメンおばさんと姪のソフィ（15歳）は、朝早くオアハカの市場にある小さな食堂（フォンダ）に着きます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Aunt Carmen and her niece Sofi, 15 years old, arrive early at a small eatery in the Oaxaca market.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: El puesto de doña Eustolia está al fondo, y ella sirve el café de olla bien caliente en un jarro de barro.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Doña Eustolia's stall is at the back, and she serves the café de olla very hot in a clay mug.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: ドニャ・エウストリアの売り場は市場の奥にあり、彼女はカフェ・デ・オジャを陶器のマグに入れ、とても熱い状態で出します。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Doña Eustolia's stall is at the back, and she serves the café de olla very hot in a clay mug.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Carmen quiere que Sofi pida sola por primera vez, así que la prepara en la banca de la fonda.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Carmen wants Sofi to order alone for the first time, so she coaches her on the eatery's bench.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメンはソフィに初めて一人で注文してほしいので、食堂のベンチでやり方を教えます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Carmen wants Sofi to order alone for the first time, so she coaches her on the eatery's bench.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Carmen
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Carmen: Salúdala primero y háblale de usted.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Carmen: Greet her first and speak to her formally.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメン：まずあいさつして、それから丁寧な言葉で話しかけてね。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Carmen: Greet her first and speak to her formally.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Carmen
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Carmen: Dile así: Buenos días, doña Eustolia, ¿me da un café de olla?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Carmen: Say it like this: Good morning, doña Eustolia, may I have a café de olla?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメン：こう言ってね。「おはようございます、ドニャ・エウストリア。カフェ・デ・オジャを一杯いただけますか。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Carmen: Say it like this: Good morning, doña Eustolia, may I have a café de olla?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Sofi pregunta si el café es muy dulce, y Carmen le explica que doña Eustolia lo prepara con piloncillo y canela.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Sofi asks if the coffee is very sweet, and Carmen explains that doña Eustolia makes it with piloncillo and cinnamon.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: ソフィがそのコーヒーはとても甘いのかとたずねると、カルメンは、ドニャ・エウストリアはピロンシージョ（円すい形の黒砂糖）とシナモンで作っていると説明します。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Sofi asks if the coffee is very sweet, and Carmen explains that doña Eustolia makes it with piloncillo and cinnamon.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Carmen
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Carmen: Pídelo sin piloncillo si no lo quieres tan dulce.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Carmen: Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメン：あまり甘くないのがよければ、ピロンシージョなしで頼んでね。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Carmen: Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Carmen
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Carmen: Si prefieres otra cosa, pide un chocolate de agua, que también es muy rico.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Carmen: If you'd rather have something else, order a hot chocolate made with water, which is also really good.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメン：ほかのものがよければ、水で作るホットチョコレート（チョコラテ・デ・アグア）を頼んでね。それもすごくおいしいから。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Carmen: If you'd rather have something else, order a hot chocolate made with water, which is also really good.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Carmen
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Carmen: Escoge un pan de yema y pídeselo a doña Eustolia con el café.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Carmen: Pick a pan de yema and ask doña Eustolia for it with the coffee.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメン：パン・デ・ジェマ（卵黄のパン）を選んで、コーヒーといっしょにドニャ・エウストリアに頼んでね。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Carmen: Pick a pan de yema and ask doña Eustolia for it with the coffee.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Carmen
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Carmen: Pregúntale cuánto es y págale con el billete de 50.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Carmen: Ask her how much it is and pay her with the 50-peso bill.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメン：いくらか聞いて、50ペソ札で払ってね。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Carmen: Ask her how much it is and pay her with the 50-peso bill.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Carmen
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Carmen: Si te da monedas de cambio, guárdalas en la bolsa del pantalón.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Carmen: If she gives you coins as change, put them away in your pants pocket.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメン：おつりに小銭をもらったら、ズボンのポケットにしまってね。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Carmen: If she gives you coins as change, put them away in your pants pocket.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Carmen
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Carmen: Agárralo por el asa, nunca por el borde.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Carmen: Hold it by the handle, never by the rim.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメン：取っ手を持って。マグのふちは絶対に持たないでね。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Carmen: Hold it by the handle, never by the rim.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Carmen
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Carmen: No lo toques todavía; espera a que deje de echar vapor.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Carmen: Don't touch it yet; wait until it stops steaming.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメン：まだ触らないで。湯気が出なくなるまで待ってね。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Carmen: Don't touch it yet; wait until it stops steaming.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Carmen
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Carmen: Si sigue muy caliente, déjalo en la mesa hasta que esté tibio.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Carmen: If it's still very hot, leave it on the table until it's lukewarm.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメン：まだすごく熱かったら、ぬるくなるまでテーブルに置いておいてね。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Carmen: If it's still very hot, leave it on the table until it's lukewarm.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Carmen
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Carmen: Pruébalo despacito, porque el barro guarda el calor.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Carmen: Taste it slowly, because the clay holds the heat.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメン：ゆっくり少しずつ味わってね。陶器の器は熱を保つから。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Carmen: Taste it slowly, because the clay holds the heat.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Carmen
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Carmen: Tú puedes, yo te espero aquí en la banca.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Carmen: You've got this, I'll wait for you here on the bench.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: カルメン：ソフィならできるよ。私はここのベンチで待ってるね。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Carmen: You've got this, I'll wait for you here on the bench.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Sofi camina sola al puesto, saluda a doña Eustolia y pide su café de olla con su pan de yema.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Sofi walks to the stall alone, greets doña Eustolia and orders her café de olla with her pan de yema.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: ソフィは一人で売り場まで歩いていき、ドニャ・エウストリアにあいさつして、カフェ・デ・オジャとパン・デ・ジェマを注文します。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Sofi walks to the stall alone, greets doña Eustolia and orders her café de olla with her pan de yema.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Minutos después, Sofi regresa a la banca con el jarro bien agarrado por el asa y su pan en la otra mano.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Minutes later, Sofi comes back to the bench holding the mug firmly by the handle, with her bread in her other hand.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 数分後、ソフィはマグの取っ手をしっかり持ち、もう片方の手にパンを持って、ベンチに戻ってきます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Minutes later, Sofi comes back to the bench holding the mug firmly by the handle, with her bread in her other hand.

speakingGoalInternal: You are the aunt or uncle, and the AI is your 15-year-old niece Sofi: coach her to order café de olla and a pan dulce on her own, using commands with pronouns like pídelo, agárralo por el asa and no lo toques todavía.
speakingGoalJapaneseDraft: あなたはソフィのおばさん（またはおじさん）です。AIは15歳の姪のソフィです。ソフィが一人でカフェ・デ・オジャと甘いパン（この場面ではパン・デ・ジェマ）を注文できるように、「ピロンシージョなしで頼んでね」「取っ手を持ってね」「まだ触らないでね」のような短い指示で教えてあげてください。

savedPositionPolicy: Archived draft rows have no explicit stable row IDs and were not registered. Revision-scoped candidate IDs do not authorize saved-item or audio placement migration. Reordering requires a new revision.
reviewQuestionsInternal: Archive lessons[2] diverges from the Spanish source (hot cocoa at a generic café, no Oaxaca, no Carmen/Sofi/doña Eustolia, no pan de yema, no 50-peso bill, Adult/Teen/Staff speakers); not reused.
Card order follows the Spanish words array: 15 terms then 8 phrases; all glossEn values equal the exact English source rows.
Reader has 18 rows; Carmen rows keep the 'カルメン：' marker, narration rows have no speaker label; Sofi has no spoken Reader line.
Spanish usted has no direct Japanese equivalent; 'speak to her formally' is rendered 丁寧な言葉で話しかけて; reviewer should decide between 敬語 and 丁寧語 for a 15-year-old learner.
Carmen's lines to her niece use casual ～てね/～ないでね; the line to doña Eustolia uses polite いただけますか; reviewer to confirm tone.
The Spanish object-pronoun command grammar focus has no Japanese equivalent; the speaking goal teaches the same commands without pronoun morphology.

ドニャ is a draft katakana choice for doña; qualified review should choose the title's transliteration. Mexican food and locale names remain in katakana with English source anchors (ピロンシージョ, パン・デ・ジェマ, チョコラテ・デ・アグア, フォンダ).
The clay mug is drafted as 陶器のマグ（ハロ・デ・バロ）; qualified review should check material specificity and the Spanish name's katakana form. The market stall is drafted as 売り場, not a street cart.
'Taste it slowly' is drafted as ゆっくり少しずつ味わって and 'clay holds heat' as 陶器の器は熱を保つ. The draft adds no medical or injury claims.
The source speaking goal names pan dulce, while the specific Reader scene names pan de yema; the draft goal keeps both scopes visible for qualified source review.
Reader 13–14 keep the source's steam-stops and lukewarm waiting conditions; Reader 17–18 keep the source outcome that Sofi orders and returns, with nothing invented.
